correctness.rationale: For every \(n\ge2\), all positive rank populations and \(0\le k\le r\), completeness of the facet types follows from Lemma 3.2 of Ahmad–Fourier–Joswig. Direct Dirichlet integration gives common volume \(E/n!\), each zero/top facet \(E/[m_i(n-1)!]\), each order-equality facet \(\sqrt2 E/[m_i m_{i+1}(n-1)!]\), and each mixed facet \(\sqrt{k+1}E/[(n-1)!\prod_{i\le k+1}m_i]\). All Gram factors are derived from Euclidean graph parametrizations. Summing yields the complete profile, and square-root concavity gives strict inequalities. The pure chain endpoint is separately integrated. Independent convex-hull verification passed 253 finite cases and 2204 facet-rank checks through dimension six; the proof is not extrapolated from these finite cases.

value.rationale: The natural interpolation, previously studied for monotone face numbers, instead has nonincreasing ordinary Euclidean boundary area at exactly equal volume. The complete intermediate surface-area ratio is independent of rank populations despite widely varying facet counts and individual areas. The endpoint fractional reduction tends to \(1-1/\sqrt2\) as the number of ranks grows. This is a motivated structural metric law for the whole interpolation, not an increment to a known endpoint number.
